audit.whatIsWrong: The entry calls Olaf's W 'Vicious Strikes' and describes it as lifesteal, in six places (whys[0], whys[6], spikes[0].text, early, late, wants.foe[2]). Olaf's W is Tough It Out: 'Olaf's Attack Speed is increased and he gains a Shield.' The lifesteal comes from his passive, Berserker Rage, scaling with missing Health.
audit.why: Vicious Strikes is the old pre-rework W. Naming it that AND attributing the sustain to the wrong ability changes the play: the player is told to out-damage a lifesteal button that does not exist, instead of forcing out a burst-absorbing shield and punishing him at high HP when his passive lifesteal is at its weakest.
audit.corrected: W is Tough It Out — attack speed plus a shield, 16/15/14/13/12s. Sustain is Berserker Rage, and it scales UP as he drops low, so a long grind favours him and a burst window at full HP favours you.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two claims about Irelia's own kit are wrong: the passive is credited with 'armor/MR shred' or 'resist-shred' five times, and W (Defiant Dance) is described as eating 'his biggest hit'.
audit.why: Ionian Fervor is stacking Attack Speed plus bonus on-hit damage at max stacks — no shred. Defiant Dance reduces PHYSICAL damage only, and Olaf's biggest hit is Reckless Swing, which is true damage: neither armour nor Defiant Dance touches it. Telling the player to 'build armor' and W his burst is actively wrong in this matchup.
audit.corrected: Passive = attack speed / on-hit. Against Reckless Swing nothing mitigates — the answer is to end the fight, not to tank it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven chart rows disagreed with their own whys text and with the packet chart. whys[2] calls Level 3 'your first spike' while the row read Olaf; whys[3] says 'you out-duel him at 4-5' while the row read Skill; whys[5] says 'making you the lane tyrant' while the row read Olaf.
audit.why: The packet chart (Olaf, Skill, Irelia, Irelia, Skill, Irelia, Olaf) matches the prose exactly.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 2, 3, 5 flipped in matched full/content pairs, with row 1 and row 4 ratings brought to 5/10 for the even stages.

audit.whatIsWrong: First-item spike named Trinity Force in whys[5], spikes[2].text, late and wants.you[2], while the itemization block builds Blade of the Ruined King.
audit.why: Self-contradiction on one page. Ragnarok's 100/90/80s cooldown is the other spike that matters and is stated correctly.
audit.corrected: All four renamed to Blade of the Ruined King.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1] told the player to 'walk over his axe to deny it'. Only Olaf can retrieve Undertow — Irelia cannot deny the pickup by standing on it.
audit.why: Riot text: 'If Olaf picks up the axe, the ability's cooldown is reset.' The playable version is to fight away from where the axe landed so retrieving it costs him position.
audit.corrected: Title and body rewritten; Undertow's flat 9s cooldown and armour reduction stated.

edits.before: Level 1 belongs to Olaf — his thrown axe (Q) slows you and W (Vicious Strikes) heals back your chip, so he out-trades your stunless level-1 Irelia that only has a single-target Q. Just farm with Bladesurge, and when he throws an axe to slow you, sidestep it so he has to walk over to pick it up for the cooldown reset — deny that and the trade stays neutral. Don't walk up to last-hit into a free axe slow. Your turn comes at level 3: with E (Flawless Duet) online you can finally E-stun into a Q and punish him in the window right after he's committed and thrown his axe away.
edits.after: Level 1 belongs to Olaf — Undertow (Q) slows you and cuts your armour while his Berserker Rage lifesteal heals back your chip, so he out-trades your stunless level-1 Irelia that only has a single-target Q. Just farm with Bladesurge, and when he throws an axe, step away from where it lands so he has to walk over to pick it up and reset that flat 9s cooldown — cost him the walk and the trade stays neutral. Don't last-hit into a free axe slow. Your turn comes at level 3: with E (Flawless Duet) online you can E-stun into a Q and punish him in the window right after he's thrown the axe away.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are a real skirmish window — your Bladesurge resets and passive stacks ramp once a fight goes long, so E-stun, Q in, and let the on-hit magic and armor/MR shred build while your W (Defiant Dance) damage-reduction channel eats his biggest hit. The whole mid-game pivots on his Ragnarok (R): if it's down you win the all-in cleanly, but if it's up he turns CC-immune the moment you E, so the stun whiffs and his Reckless Swing (E) true damage chunks you through your armor. Check his R cooldown or bait it out before you ever commit your E.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are a real skirmish window — your Bladesurge resets and Ionian Fervor stacks ramp once a fight goes long, so E-stun, Q in, and let the attack speed and bonus on-hit build. Force out Tough It Out (W) first: it is a shield plus attack speed on a 16s rank-1 cooldown and it eats your burst. The whole lane pivots on Ragnarok (R): down, you win the all-in cleanly; up, he is immune to disables while he keeps attacking, so the stun whiffs and Reckless Swing (E) true damage chunks you — armour and Defiant Dance's physical cut do nothing to it.

edits.before: Your first-item spike (Trinity/bruiser core) is your single strongest point — Bladesurge reset uptime, maxed passive resist-shred, and your W damage reduction make you a lane tyrant, so force every all-in here while his Ragnarok is on cooldown. But Olaf out-scales you at two items: his W lifesteal sustain climbs and his Reckless Swing (E) true damage ignores the armor your build leans on, while his Ragnarok means you can never reliably lock him down with E. Convert your early lead into plates, the first turret, and grubs — don't let this drift into a late 1v1 where his R blanks your only hard CC.
edits.after: Blade of the Ruined King is your single strongest point — Bladesurge reset uptime, max Ionian Fervor attack speed and %HP damage make you a lane tyrant, so force every all-in here while his Ragnarok is on cooldown. But Olaf out-scales you at two items: Berserker Rage lifesteals harder the lower he drops, and Reckless Swing (E) true damage ignores the armor your build leans on, while Ragnarok means you can never reliably lock him down with E. Convert your early lead into plates, the first turret, and grubs — don't let this drift into a late 1v1 where his R blanks your only hard CC.

notes: Biggest find in this slice so far: the entry used Olaf's PRE-REWORK W, 'Vicious Strikes', six times and attributed his lifesteal to it. Data Dragon has W = Tough It Out (attack speed + shield); the lifesteal is Berserker Rage (passive), scaling with MISSING health. That inversion matters — the old text implies grinding him down is safe, when in fact his sustain gets stronger the lower he goes and the shield is what blocks your burst. Also corrected: 'build armor' and 'W his burst' advice against Reckless Swing, which is true damage that neither armour nor Defiant Dance's physical-only reduction affects. Chart flipped to the packet chart, which already agreed with the whys prose on all seven rows.
